title_short: Application of Rational Emotive Behavioral Therapy (REBT) in the Treatment of Examination Cheating Behavior among Students
journal_or_source: Journal of Academic Ethics (2025) 23:503-522; doi:10.1007/s10805-025-09596-1 (accepted 9 Jan 2025; published online 24 Jan 2025)
linked_reports_noted: Dataset: Ocheni et al. (2024) Examination cheating behavior data, Science Data Bank, https://cstr.cn/31253.11.sciencedb.08210 (Data Availability p.519). No other linked reports noted.
design: quasi-experimental non-randomised (author-labelled pre-test, post-test non-equivalent control group quasi-experimental design; 'randomization is not possible since the students are in intact classes') (Abstract; Methods Design p.507); however two intact classes were 'randomly assigned' to REBT and CC (p.508 Participants; p.511 Procedures) - i.e. 1 class per arm; see integrity_notes
allocation_unit: class (intact class; one class from each of two schools)
n_clusters_per_arm: 1 class (1 school) per arm (p.508 Participants: two intact classes from two schools)
randomisation_method: Intact classes 'randomly assigned' to experimental (REBT) and control (CC); method of random assignment NR; schools selected by purposive sampling; allocation concealment NR; blinding NR (p.508; p.511)
geopolitical_zone: South East (derived from Enugu State; report says only 'eastern region of Nigeria' p.507)
school_type: NR (public/private NR; schools described as 'mixed (male and female)' i.e. co-educational) (p.508)
population_notes: All senior secondary students in mixed-sex schools in Nsukka LGA = population; 67 students from two intact classes in two schools (purposive school selection to ensure both genders). No screening or inclusion threshold on examination cheating behaviour reported. Pretest ECBS means high in both arms (REBT 65.21, CC 62.69 on 20-80 scale). Age not reported despite text stating age described (p.511). Incentive: box of cookies each session (Ethical Approval).
prevention_level: universal (intact classes; no screening or selection on examination cheating behaviour reported, p.508) - reviewer judgement, not author-stated
age_mean_sd_range: NR (Data Analysis p.511 says age was described with frequency counts, but no age data reported)
pct_female: Overall % NR; 32 of 67 female (REBT 12/28; CC 20/39) (Abstract; p.508; Table 3: REBT females 17.9% of total, CC females 29.9% of total)
n_analysed_total: 67 (REBT 28; CC 39) (Table 4; Table 5 Total 67, Corrected Total df 66, Error df 62); text p.514 gives CC posttest n=28, contradicting Table 4 and Table 7 subgroup n (19+20=39) - treated as typo (see integrity_notes)
intervention_name: Rational Emotive Behavioral Therapy (REBT), ABC-DEF model
intervention_components: Manualised ABC-DEF model in six stages: A activating events about examination cheating; B beliefs about cheating as irrational; C consequences of cheating; D disputing/restructuring irrational beliefs; E creating effective new beliefs/behaviours to minimise cheating; F feeling better by incorporating new rational beliefs. Introductory session on REBT concept, rules and duration. Therapist-led discussion and illustrations (p.509 Treatment Manual; Table 1)
sessions_n: 8 (two sessions a week for four weeks) (p.511 Experimental Procedures; p.509); see integrity_notes re schedule inconsistency
duration_weeks: 4 weeks of intervention (5 weeks in total including 1 week training of research assistants) (Abstract; p.509; p.511)
delivery_agent: researcher or psychologist (REBT delivered by an educational psychologist, PhD, trained in REBT, aged 36; CC by an educational counsellor, PhD, aged 38; both called research assistants/therapists) (p.509 Therapists; p.511)
format: group (delivered to intact class; group format implied, not explicitly stated)
setting_detail: School premises (intact classes in the two sampled schools); whether in school hours NR; March 2024 (p.511)
comparator_type: usual curriculum or conventional counselling (manualised conventional counselling, labelled control group)
comparator_detail: Conventional counselling (CC), 5-stage model based on Sutton (2021): relationship building; in-depth exploration/problem assessment on examination cheating; commitment to action/goal setting; counselling intervention (resources, activities, exercises to alter cheating behaviour); evaluation/termination. Delivered by an educational counsellor (PhD, aged 38); same 8 x 60-min schedule (p.509; Table 1; p.511). Authors chose CC as 'standard treatment' control (p.507).
outcomes_and_tools: Examination cheating behaviour: Examination Cheating Behavior Scale (ECBS), researcher-developed, 20 items, 4-point Likert (1 strongly disagree to 4 strongly agree), range 20-80, Cronbach alpha 0.86 (pilot n=25); higher = more cheating behaviour (inferred from authors' interpretation of decrease as improvement; direction not explicitly stated) (p.508 Measures; Abstract)
timepoints: baseline (pretest); post (immediately after the 4-week intervention); no follow-up (p.511)
analysis_method: ANCOVA (posttest DV, pretest covariate; factors intervention, gender, intervention x gender), SPSS v23; descriptives, chi-square; clustering accounted: no (individual-level analysis with 1 class per arm) (p.511 Data Analysis; Table 5)
attrition: NR explicitly; all 67 apparently analysed (Table 4; Table 5 df)
fidelity_acceptability: Treatment integrity: assessor (senior lecturer, Dept of Educational Research, Measurement and Evaluation, UNN) monitored process, recorded attendance of research assistants and students and ensured manuals were used (p.508 Treatment Integrity; p.511); attendance data not reported; acceptability NR
trial_registration: NR (ethics approval: Research and Ethics Committee, University of Nigeria, Nsukka; informed consent obtained)
integrity_notes: (1) Table 6 (by gender, arms pooled) reproduces Table 4 (by arm) values exactly: Male pre 65.21/6.43, post 39.21/12.72, gain 26.00 = REBT; Female pre 62.69/6.70, post 55.36/8.95, gain 7.33 = CC, despite different n (35/32 vs 28/39) and inconsistency with Table 7 cells (Table 4 arm means are consistent with Table 7 cells; Table 6 is not); only adjusted means differ (43.11/1.29; 53.18/1.39) - copied/impossible values. (2) Text p.514 gives CC posttest n=28 vs n=39 in Table 4 and Table 7. (3) 'SDadj' for adjusted means (1.23-2.19) are of SE magnitude, labelled SD. (4) Levene test Table 2 p=.070 but text p.512 reports 'p > 0.50'. (5) Chi-square reported as chi2(1)=.464, p=.621 (Table 3; p.512); p appears inconsistent with chi2=.464 on 1 df (would be approx. .50). (6) Session schedule inconsistent: p.509 says week 1 training, week 2 introduction, two sessions a week for remaining three weeks (eight sessions, five weeks), while p.511 says four weeks of intervention x 2 sessions = 8 sessions; Table 1 lists 5 weeks. (7) Design described as non-randomised quasi-experimental ('randomization is not possible', p.507) yet intact classes 'randomly assigned' (p.508, p.511); one class per arm in different schools, so arm fully confounded with school/class; unit-of-analysis error (individual-level ANCOVA, clustering ignored, ICC NR). (8) Pretest covariate non-significant in ANCOVA (F=1.006, p=.320) despite pre-post design. (9) Partial eta squared misinterpreted as '% reduction in examination cheating' (p.514-516). (10) Different therapist per arm (therapist confounded with arm). (11) Gender main effect discussed as REBT being more potent for males, but Table 5 gender effect is pooled across arms. (12) Baseline imbalance in subgroups: REBT male pre 66.81 vs CC male 61.84 (Table 7). (13) Implausibly large REBT male effect (pre 66.81/SD 4.26 to post 29.25/SD 3.28; near scale floor of 20) vs small change in CC males (61.84 to 56.79).
notes: Outcome is examination cheating behaviour (academic dishonesty), coded under aggression_conduct_behaviour per protocol instruction. Both arms received active manualised interventions (REBT vs conventional counselling). Gender-by-arm subgroup data in Table 7; ANCOVA interaction F(1,62)=42.701. Population not screened for cheating; Nsukka, Enugu. Training of research assistants last week of February 2024; intervention from March 2024 (p.511). Incentive: box of cookies each session (p.519). Authors affiliated with University of Alabama (USA) and University of Nigeria, Nsukka.
reconciliation_notes: 37 of 45 File A fields differed between extractors; 6 substantive and resolved against full text (first_author format, prevention_level [x2 NR vs x1 universal: universal as reviewer judgement], pct_female/n_analysed_total wording [both 32/67 and 67; CC n=28 in text p.514 confirmed typo against Table 4/Table 7], integrity_notes [merged: x1 items plus x2 baseline-imbalance and implausible-effect items; chi-square p inconsistency confirmed], notes [merged dates/incentive]); remaining differences were wording/detail only, X1 wording kept with page refs verified. Usable outcome data: YES (arm n, mean, SD at baseline and post, Table 4), with serious integrity concerns (Table 6 duplication, 1 cluster per arm).
